newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Sept 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Arab League's ministerial council called on Iran to end its occupation of islands belonging to the UAE.
The council was referring to the Greater and Lesser Tunbs and Abu Musa, three Gulf islands disputed by the UAE and Iran.
- United Arab Emirates special forces arrived in Bahrain on Sunday for military exercises with Bahrain's armed forces.
- The Emirates and Belarus are discussing two investment protection deals.
- The general director of the Dubai Chamber of Commerce discussed opportunities for investment with a delegation from Thailand.
- Saudi Arabia considers a fresh U.S. strike against Iraq unlikely, the Saudi minister of defence said.
- A Grindlays Bank study predicted economic growth in the UAE due to increased oil and gas capacity in Abu Dhabi and Dubai's focus on trade.
- Top officials from Germany's Dresdner Bank called on Gulf states to lift 49 percent foreign ownership restrictions to encourage investment.

- The Gulf states will soon have a unified office for the registration of patents as part of collective measures to tighten intellectual property laws. The new office at the GCC General Secretariat in Riyadh is to open for registration by November.
- Fifty-four Western, Arab and Asian banks on Sunday agreed to lend $1.2 billion to a U.S.-Kuwaiti joint venture to build a petrochemical complex in the Gulf state.
- The UAE imported about $1 billion worth of goods from Japan during the first half of the year, the Japan External Trade Organsiation said on Sunday.
